title: What to Know About Djibouti’s Refugee Crisis
gist: Africa Brief: Houthi gains (Mokha, Mayun/Perim Island) put the rebels 12 miles from Djibouti, driving 3,000+ Yemeni refugees there with UNHCR warning of 10,000, and turning Djibouti's base-leasing location into a liability. Houthi-al-Shabab cooperation and piracy (al-Shabab taking 20-30% of ransoms) threaten a transregional war; also Ethiopia's renewed Tigray war, U.S. lifting Eritrea sanctions, Morocco's election, and Dangote becoming Europe's top jet fuel supplier.

insights.claim: Houthi capture of Mokha and Mayun (Perim) Island puts the group just 12 miles from Djibouti's coast on the Bab el-Mandeb, which handles about 12 percent of global maritime trade.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Escalating chokepoint risk for Red Sea shipping, freight rates and insurance.
insights.quote: The Houthi’s recent capture of Yemen’s port city of Mokha and the strategic Mayun Island (also called Perim) has now put the rebel group just 12 miles from Djibouti’s coast.
insights.locator: Djibouti sits directly across from Yemen

insights.claim: More than 3,000 Yemeni refugees have reached Djibouti in recent weeks, and UNHCR warns this could hit 10,000 as sea conditions improve after mid-October; its Djibouti operation is only 15 percent funded.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Humanitarian strain on a key logistics/basing hub.

insights.claim: Djibouti's strategic location, long monetized by leasing land to U.S., Chinese, Japanese and European militaries, is becoming a liability amid the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Risk to Djibouti's port-and-basing economic model.
insights.quote: But Djibouti’s strategic position has increasingly become a liability as it faces rising fallout from the Iran war.

insights.claim: Rising Houthi attacks may restrict shipping around Djibouti's port, which carries about 97 percent of Ethiopia's cargo, potentially pushing Abiy to renew his bid for sea access via Eritrea.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Raises Ethiopia-Eritrea war risk and Ethiopian trade disruption.
insights.quote: which Ethiopia relies on for around 97 percent of its cargo

insights.claim: The Houthis and al-Shabab have drastically expanded military cooperation, raising risks of transregional war across the Horn of Africa and arms-smuggling lifelines for both.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Broader Red Sea/Gulf of Aden insecurity, extending shipping risk south.
insights.locator: In recent months, the Houthis and al-Shabab

insights.claim: As naval attacks pushed shipping closer to Somalia, piracy resurged and al-Shabab reportedly takes a 20 to 30 percent cut of ransom payments.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Rerouted shipping faces piracy risk, raising insurance and security costs.
insights.quote: taking an estimated 20 percent to 30 percent cut of ransom payments

insights.claim: Washington gave the U.N. another year to phase out its $550 million logistical support for AU peacekeepers in Somalia, after warnings fast removal would weaken defenses against al-Shabab.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Short reprieve for Somalia security; cliff risk in a year.
insights.locator: Nearly two decades of U.S. security

insights.claim: Israel's recognition of Somaliland, likely partly to monitor the Houthis, may heighten regional insecurity and turbocharge Houthi-al-Shabab ties.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Recognition politics add to Horn of Africa escalation risk.

insights.claim: TPLF rebels seized airports in Mekelle, Shire and Axum and formed an 'Alliance for Survival' with six armed groups to overthrow Abiy's government, fueling fears of renewed all-out war.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Renewed Ethiopian civil war risk for a large frontier economy.

insights.claim: The U.S. lifted sanctions on Eritrea's ruling party and military to court its Assab port near the Bab el-Mandeb, indirectly escalating Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Red Sea strategy is driving U.S. realignment in the Horn.

insights.claim: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery has become Europe's top jet fuel supplier amid Iran-war Middle East shortages, and its IPO last week was the biggest in Africa's history.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Dangote is a key beneficiary of Middle East product disruption and a major new listed African asset.
insights.quote: Nigeria’s Dangote Refinery, a private company based in the outskirts of Lagos, has become Europe’s top supplier of jet fuel in recent months

insights.claim: Morocco's parliamentary election is expected to produce a PAM win amid youth discontent, with RNI promising 1 million jobs after Akhannouch stepped back.
insights.speaker: Nosmot Gbadamosi
insights.so_what: Political transition risk in Morocco is contained by monarchy's ultimate power.
insights.locator: Yet political observers expect a PAM win
